world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length) Contrasting tones or tone patterns are not in evidence. Stress is unpredictable but non-contrastive. Closed syllables and syllables with lengthened vowels are often but not always stressed. [examples, p. 7:] [ˈwa.ka] /waka/ 'ruined', [gɪ.ˈfi] /gifi/ 'skin', [ɪn.ˈtɛ] /intɛ/ 'song', [bɪ.ni.ˈfɪn] /binifin/ 'middle', [ɔ.ˈɾɔp̚] /ɔɾɔp/ 'great', [ˈwɪn.tɪ.fi] /wintifi/ 'lightning', [bɪs.a.ɾa.ˈmi] /bisaɾami/ 'little', [fɪ.ˈfi:] /fifii/ 'fly', [ˈgu:.mu] /guumu/ 'down there', [ˈmɛ.nɛ:] /mɛnɛɛ/ 'thorn'. Length is contrastive due to the fact that Finongan has a set of long vowels contrasting with a set of short vowels.

Closed syllables and syllables with lengthened vowels are often but not always stressed.' -- word for word as quoted. P. 7 continues with exactly the ten stress-marked examples listed in the report ([ˈwa.ka] 'ruined', [gɪ.ˈfi] 'skin', [ɪn.ˈtɛ] 'song', [bɪ.ni.ˈfɪn] 'middle', [ɔ.ˈɾɔp̚] 'great', [ˈwɪn.tɪ.fi] 'lightning', [bɪs.a.ɾa.ˈmi] 'litt…
new_statements.rule_in_words: No tone. Word stress placement is described as not predictable by rule yet not used contrastively (no minimal pairs by stress); there is a tendency for heavy syllables (closed or long-vowel) to attract stress, but the authors say this is not consistent. Transcribed examples show stress on initial, final and medial syllables of di- and trisyllables. Vowel length, not stress, is the contrastive suprasegmental.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned; transcriptions mark only one (primary) stress per word.
new_statements.exceptions: The heavy-syllable tendency is explicitly 'often but not always' (e.g. [ˈmɛ.nɛ:] 'thorn' and [ˈgu:.mu] vs [fɪ.ˈfi:] 'fly'); no further conditioning given.
new_statements.domain_note: Statements and transcriptions concern isolated citation forms of words in an SIL Organised Phonology Data sheet; no discussion of phrase-level prosody. Data mainly from Bakame village (Bakame-Kalange dialect).
new_statements.identity_note: The OPD describes Finongan [fag] = fino1238 as a whole, with data collected mainly in Bakame village (Bakame/Kalange dialect); the Mama village dialect differs 'mainly phonologically' per the 2015 dictionary introduction but is not separately described. Older literature calls the language Finungwan/Finungwa.

sources.note: p. 6 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)': no contrastive tone; 'Stress is unpredictable but non-contrastive. Closed syllables and syllables with lengthened vowels are often but not always stressed.' Length is contrastive. Phonetic transcriptions throughout mark primary stress, on varying syllables (e.g. [ˈa.pu] 'sugar', [am.ˈbi] 'lime', [bɪ.ni.ˈfɪn] 'middle', [ˈwɪn.tɪ.fi] 'lightning', [bɪs.a.ɾa.ˈmi] 'little').
